column1: # Integration fixture shapes, per package — MEASURED, not assumed.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
#   Round 44 §7 found that the integration-only test files fall into families
#   that cannot share one database: some build their own schema (and collide
#   with a populated one), some assume an already-migrated one (and fail on an
#   empty one). One harness could only build one kind of database, so it could
#   only ever serve half of them.
#   This file records, per package, which shape the harness should build.
#   run-integration-gate.sh reads it; GATE_DB_SHAPE=... overrides it.
# ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS FILE
#   **A shape label is NOT a green light.** Measured 2026-10-01 by running the
#   same package on both shapes, no package is green on either. The two fixture
#   families are interleaved INSIDE packages, not separated by them.
#   That is a correction to R44 §7, which described the split as if it were
#   clean. It is not.
#   ⚠ SCOPE OF THE MEASUREMENT, stated exactly so nobody reads it as broader
#   than it is. A full 27-package sweep on the prereqs shape was started and
#   **stopped at 6/27** because `db` HUNG on that shape (log frozen, process at
#   0% CPU, killed by hand) — itself a stronger negative signal than a failure.
#   So:
#     * 3 packages measured on BOTH shapes this session:
#         taskprofile              installer 2 FAIL  ->  prereqs 1 FAIL
#         bg                       installer 14 FAIL ->  prereqs VACUOUS (0 PASS)
#         sql/migrations/startup   installer 6 FAIL  ->  prereqs 5 FAIL
#     * 5 more measured on prereqs, compared against the earlier full sweep:
#         admin        11 FAIL -> 66 FAIL
#         autoupdate    0 FAIL -> 16 FAIL
#         center        0 FAIL -> 10 FAIL
#         cmd-gateway   0 FAIL ->  0 FAIL   (only package unaffected)
#         db            0 FAIL ->  HUNG
#   NOT measured on prereqs: the other 19 packages. Do not assume their numbers.
#   Re-run to extend; the sweep is a plain loop, see HOW TO REGENERATE.
#   Reading: prereqs removes a 42P07 or two per package but ADDS failures
#   elsewhere in the same package, because the other half of those tests
#   assumes a migrated database. **Switching shape moves failures around; it
#   does not remove them.** The per-shape FAIL columns below are what stop the
#   next reader from reading "taskprofile -> prereqs" as "switching fixed it".
#   It did not.
# WHY A WHOLE-DATABASE SHAPE IS THE WRONG AXIS (and what replaces it)
#   The harness's unit is a package, but the fixture families are finer than a
#   package. The fix that actually separates them is per-test isolation: give
#   each self-building test its own schema (`CREATE SCHEMA ... ; SET
#   search_path`) inside the populated database, so it neither collides with
#   the baseline nor needs a second database.
#   There is no shared helper for that in this repo yet — three files hand-roll
#   `CREATE SCHEMA` (tools/benchreport/main.go,
#   domains/reportrollup/grainreport_e2e_test.go,
#   sql/migrations/startup/migration_536_540_integration_test.go). Building
#   `testschema.New(t, pool)` and migrating the self-building files onto it is
#   the real work, and it is deliberately NOT done here: it touches ~30 files
#   and is a separate batch. Tracked in
#   docs/audit/2026-10-01-round44-closure-fixtures.md.
# HOW TO REGENERATE
#   GATE_DB_SHAPE=prereqs  bash scripts/audit/run-integration-gate.sh <pkg>
#   (unset for installer; the [populated] line prints shape= and relations=)
#   Then update the shape and the two FAIL counts from the two runs.
#   A package with no row here defaults to `installer` — i.e. adding this file
#   changed nothing until someone filled a row in.
# FORMAT
#   <package-relative-path><TAB><shape><TAB><fail installer><TAB><fail prereqs><TAB><reason>
#   Sorted by package. No header, no blank lines. Both shape columns measured.
#   This file intentionally ships EMPTY. It is a shape registry with the
#   measurement harness around it; the rows are filled once the per-test
#   isolation helper exists, because until then every row would have to say
#   "neither shape works", which is true of all 27 packages and therefore
#   carries no routing information.
